thread:
maria-sales: Hey team — Enterprise prospect (FinSys) is asking for final commit sizing and a preheat/runbook for their POC. They expect 180 RPS sustained with 1.5s avg gen but spiky bursts up to 350 RPS for short windows. Need reserved GPUs + autoscale fallback. Can we draft a concise runbook?

josh-eng: Thanks — couple quick Qs: what's their model (context, quantized)? long-contexts?

maria-sales: They've been testing a 13B quantized model with 8k context. Most requests average 250 tokens, but there are occasional 2k-token generations.

sasha-ml: For 13B q4_0-ish, rough baseline: one A100-ish instance handles ~60-80 RPS for 250-token median at our infra config. Long contexts drop throughput; 2k tokens ~ 0.3x throughput.

oliver-sre: Recommended approach: reserve baseline capacity to cover 180 RPS sustained (so ~3 nodes if 60 RPS/node) + autoscale pool for burst to 350 RPS (add 2-3 burst GPUs). Also AZ spread 2x for failover.

raj-platform: I'll propose the reserved SKU: 3 dedicated GPUs (vCPU pairing + prewarmed containers) + autoscale group with spot/burst credits for 2 more. Preheat strategy: persistent KV cache and a small pool of warm workers.

maria-sales: Pricing question from FinSys: how do reserved vs burst credits show up on invoice? they want predictable monthly charge but still want burst headroom.

raj-platform: We can offer a hybrid: committed reserved capacity (monthly) for baseline, plus a capped burst-credit bucket (monthly allotment) billed at reduced burst rate. We should document headroom, burn rate, and overage alerts.

anna-legal: Heads up — they flagged a legal blocker in the questionnaire: need an architecture/data flow diagram showing no PII persists on our GPUs and KMS key control for models. Also want SLA language around preheat time and eviction fallback.

oliver-sre: For the runbook we should include: canary deploy, KV warmup script, traffic-shaping policy, and fallback model variants (smaller model) to maintain latency during eviction.

sasha-ml: I'll prepare guidance on warmup — recommend scripted prefix replay for top 50 prompt templates. Example:

```
# kv-warmup.sh (example)
for prompt in $(cat top50_prompts.txt); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d "{\"model\":\"13b-q\",\"input\":\"$prompt\"}" https://api.redwood.example/generate > /dev/null
done
```

raj-platform: Autoscale policy snippet (conceptual):

```
scale_policy:
  baseline: 3
  scale_up_threshold: 70% gpu_util
  scale_up_step: +1
  max_pool: 6
  cooldown: 90s
  az_spread: true
  fallback: route_to_smaller_model
```

maria-sales: Perfect. Can someone draft a short one-pager + runbook that I can ship to their infra and legal teams? Also they asked about oncall escalation during POC windows.

oliver-sre: Oncall: provide a dedicated oncall pager during their business hours for the first 72h of POC ramp, and a 30-min SLA for capacity-related outages. We'll include an alias (fin_poc_oncall@redwood) and an operational play:
- monitor: p95 latency, token/sec, queue depth
- action: add burst node -> if not healthy in 5m, switch to fallback model -> notify customer

anna-legal: For questionnaire items I can provide templated responses for KMS, encryption-in-transit, and SOC2 reference. Send me the DOCX they filled out and I'll flag anything requiring exec sign-off.

maria-sales: I'll attach their questionnaire and the traffic profile.

raj-platform: I'll assemble the runbook + autoscale policy + pricing options. Planning to include step-by-step preheat commands, canary checklists, and a cost table showing baseline vs burst.

josh-eng: Quick note — for long-context bursts we should recommend request-level token caps or adaptive truncation to avoid OOMs. Also recommend KV cache TTL tuning to avoid cold-start penalties.

maria-sales: Great, timeline? They want this by EOD tomorrow to close.

raj-platform: I can have a draft runbook and pricing options by EOD. Sasha will add warmup prompts, Oliver will add oncall/playbook, Anna will draft legal replies.

infra-bot: Reminder: created shared doc "FinSys_POC_Runbook_v1" at https://docs.redwood.example/FinSys_POC_Runbook_v1 (editable by #sales, #eng, #sre, #legal).

maria-sales: Thanks — I'll loop them in once draft is ready. :pray:
